subject: Agriculture
title: Antibiotic Resistance from Farms
description: A quick win: understand Antibiotic Resistance from Farms.

hook.text: More antibiotics are used on healthy animals than on sick humans. Farms are breeding superbugs.

buildup.text: Low-dose antibiotics in animal feed promote faster growth. The US livestock industry used this for decades.

discovery.text: Bacteria exposed to constant low-dose antibiotics evolve resistance—then spread to humans via food and water.

twist.text: The WHO lists antibiotic resistance as a top 10 global health threat. Farm use is a major driver.

climax.text: The EU banned growth-promoting antibiotics in 2006. The US restricted them in 2017. Many countries haven't.

punchline.text: We're trading future medicine for cheaper meat today.

quiz.question: Why are antibiotics used on healthy farm animals?
options: Low doses promote faster growth, but breed resistant bacteria

details.summary: Livestock farming uses more antibiotics globally than human medicine, accelerating the evolution of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. This topic covers how farm antibiotic use breeds superbugs, the transmission pathways to humans, and policy responses worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Antibiotic resistance kills over 1.2 million people annually and is projected to cause 10 million deaths per year by 2050. Farm antibiotic overuse is a major but addressable contributor to this global health crisis.
takeaways: About 73% of all antibiotics sold globally are used in livestock, not human medicine
Routine low-dose antibiotics in feed promote growth but breed resistant bacteria
The EU banned growth-promoting antibiotics in animal feed in 2006

faq.question: How does farm antibiotic use create resistant bacteria?
faq.answer: Routine low-dose antibiotics in animal feed kill susceptible bacteria but allow resistant strains to survive and multiply. These resistant bacteria spread to humans through meat, manure runoff into water, direct contact, and airborne transmission from farms.

faq.question: What is being done to reduce farm antibiotic use?
faq.answer: The EU banned growth-promoting antibiotics in 2006. The US restricted medically important antibiotics for growth promotion in 2017. Many countries now require veterinary prescriptions. Better hygiene, vaccines, and improved husbandry reduce the need for antibiotics.
